stories.headline: Kumamoto earthquake death toll rises to at least 13; chip-fab impact stays contained, Mitsubishi Electric still silent
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (government + wire) on the 13-dead toll; Disputed vs a single-outlet 18-dead figure
stories.one_line: PM Takaichi and multiple wires (CNN, NPR, Japan Times, UPI) now confirm at least 13 dead, up from Tuesday's 1 confirmed + 9 missing at the Nippon Paper mill (now apparently accounted for among the dead). One AP-syndicated outlet (KSAT) separately reports 18 dead, unreconciled. Renesas confirms 2 factories suspended, all employees evacuated safely, no injuries; TSMC/Sony/Tokyo Electron impact still described as limited/contained (Seoul Economic Daily, Taipei Times). Mitsubishi Electric remains silent.
stories.score_note: Death toll materially escalated even as industrial impact stays contained; two threads moving in different directions.

stories.headline: AI-chip and power-infrastructure selloff extends into a third session as Korean chipmakers fall further overnight
stories.one_line: Korea's KOSPI fell nearly 6% overnight (Yahoo Finance market-today coverage), extending Tuesday's US-session declines (AMD -8.15%, Micron -8.85%, Marvell -7.77%, this terminal's own EWY proxy -6.05%). US index futures point to continued rotation, not broadening: NQ=F roughly flat (-0.01% vs last evening's confirmed print), ES=F/RTY=F modestly higher, YM=F modestly lower. NVDA itself remained little-changed Tuesday (+0.25%). Tonight's Microsoft/Meta/Arm/Qualcomm earnings are the next concrete test.
stories.score_note: Third consecutive session of Asian AI-chip weakness; durability question now tied directly to tonight's mega-cap capex guidance.
sources: this run's own Yahoo Finance futures/equity fetch (primary)

stories.headline: FOMC decides today; Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM as hike odds reprice sharply on the overnight oil shock
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple on mechanics; odds genuinely disputed across venues (Single-reliable-source/Preliminary on each specific figure)
stories.one_line: Decision 2:00 PM ET, Warsh press conference 2:30 PM (non-SEP meeting). Hike-odds pricing disputed: one outlet cites ~38% hike odds Friday (up from 10.7% a week earlier) after an oil-shock repricing; another cites 62% hold; this system's own Mon/Tue tracking showed a calmer 64-66% hold range. Tonight's Iran attack and oil jump (see above) is a fresh input not yet reflected in any published odds reading. New forecast 2026-07-29-am-1 logged (25-35% hike probability).
stories.score_note: Week's highest-importance scheduled event, now compounded by an overnight geopolitical/oil shock landing same-day.

stories.headline: Iran fires ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan for the first time since Trump's pause; all intercepted; US-Saudi forces strike back in Iraq
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (CENTCOM, Jordan military, Saudi Defense Ministry, Iran's own IRGC/IRNA statement all corroborate)
stories.one_line: At 17:45 ET Jul 28, IRGC forces launched ballistic missiles at a CENTCOM location in Jordan -- the first missile-level attack since Friday's pause, following a run of 30+ drone attacks in 72 hours. All missiles intercepted (Jordan's own air defense downed 5); no casualties reported. CENTCOM + Saudi Arabia struck Iran-aligned groups in Iraq in response. Oil jumped ~3.5-3.6% (WTI $81.91, this run's own reconciled fetch), a fresh input landing hours before today's FOMC decision. New forecast 2026-07-29-am-2 logged on further escalation risk.
stories.score_note: Escalation of the tracked US-Iran pause story to a direct military exchange; highest-risk geopolitical development this run, two-source rule met via multiple government primary sources.

stories.headline: Iran-Ukraine Caspian incident continues: lawmaker's fresh retaliation threat, Ukraine defends the strike, Israel still silent
stories.one_line: No new strike or retaliatory action. Iranian lawmaker Ebrahim Azizi (distinct from FM Araghchi) separately warned Ukraine that 'Iran does not leave its actions unanswered.' Ukraine's ambassador to Israel defended the strike, calling the vessel's cargo (drone/missile components) 'legitimate military targets.' Neither Israel nor Ukraine has addressed Araghchi's unevidenced 'at Israel's behest' claim, unchanged from this morning.
stories.score_note: Escalation risk for the broader Iran conflict, entangled with Russia-Ukraine; watch for Iranian action.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets Aug 3 deadline on mail-ballot EO stay; separate D.C. Circuit ruling finds a related challenge premature
stories.one_line: Justice Jackson (1st Circuit circuit justice) declined an immediate administrative stay and set a 4:00pm Aug 3 response deadline for respondent states -- a scheduling order, not a merits ruling (several outlets' 'denied' framing overstates this). Separately, a D.C. Circuit panel unanimously affirmed a different challenge to the same EO was not yet ripe (USPS hasn't issued implementing regulations), voicing skepticism about the administration's authority and feasibility before November; does not affect the pending SCOTUS stay application.
stories.score_note: Live emergency Supreme Court matter with a stated response deadline; procedural progress on two fronts, no merits ruling yet.

stories.headline: Microsoft, Meta, Arm and Qualcomm report after today's close; FY27 capex framing is the real swing factor
stories.verification: Confirmed-primary on timing (this run's own Alpha Vantage/Finnhub pulls)
stories.one_line: All four report ~16:05-16:15 ET today, confirmed via this run's own Alpha Vantage/Finnhub calendar pulls (first successful primary-calendar pull since Jul 28). MSFT EPS estimates $4.21-4.33 on ~$87.6-89.4B revenue; META EPS $7.13-7.36 on ~$60.2-61.4B revenue (estimates vary by aggregator). ~95% historical beat-odds already priced in per multiple outlets; FY27 capex guidance (MSFT ran ~$72B H1 FY26 capex) is the real stock-moving variable, not the print itself. Coinbase (COIN) reports tomorrow Jul 30, not today -- corrects prior earnings-week-preview ambiguity.
stories.score_note: Direct test of AI-capex financing anxiety driving the ongoing chip-sector selloff; today's biggest earnings catalyst alongside the FOMC decision.
sources: this run's own Alpha Vantage and Finnhub calendar pulls (primary)

stories.headline: Hugging Face publishes full reconstruction of the OpenAI agent breach; AI agent finds two critical Microsoft Bing vulnerabilities
stories.one_line: Hugging Face's security team recovered ~17,600 attacker actions clustered into ~6,280 operations from the Jul 9-13 incident -- the clearest data-backed account yet. Separately, an autonomous offensive-security AI agent identified two critical (CVSS 9.8) Microsoft Bing vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-32194, CVE-2026-32191). The Agentic AI Foundation released an updated MCP spec (2026-07-28), the largest change since launch.
stories.score_note: Upgrades the tracked breach story from narrative to granular data; Bing CVE discovery is a new dual-use AI-security data point.

stories.headline: Coca-Cola refuses ransom; Anubis leaks Fairlife data; Cl0p/ShinyHunters unchanged
stories.one_line: Coca-Cola declined to pay Anubis's ransom after Monday's deadline passed; Anubis has since published ~1TB of allegedly stolen Fairlife data on its leak site. Coca-Cola confirmed data theft occurred but hasn't verified Anubis's volume claim. Resolves forecast 2026-07-27-pm-1 (leak within 72h) well inside its horizon; graded Saturday. Production status unchanged (majority of 4 US plants resumed). Cl0p/PTC Windchill and ShinyHunters/EY (deadline Jul 31) both unchanged.
stories.score_note: Ransomware extortion-deadline follow-through case study; forecast resolves same-run.

stories.headline: Arista ships VeloCloud patches ahead of CISA deadline; Origin Energy attacker claims unconfirmed settlement
stories.verification: Confirmed-multiple (Arista, CISA) / Unverified (Origin Energy settlement claim)
stories.one_line: Arista shipped patched VeloCloud Orchestrator versions (CVE-2026-16812); CISA's federal deadline remains Jul 30, exploitation continuing. CISA separately added a second Fortinet FortiOS flaw (CVE-2025-68686) to KEV, deadline Aug 10. On Origin Energy (~900,000-customer breach): the claimed attacker told an Australian outlet a private settlement was reached and no data will leak; Origin has not confirmed this -- treated as an unverified attacker claim.
stories.score_note: Patch-compliance and breach-settlement threads to watch this week.

stories.headline: Europe wildfires largely steady-state; heat wave forecast firms up slightly
stories.one_line: Bordeaux/Gironde fire (~42,000 hectares) remains 'stabilized but uncontrolled'; today's forecast heat (35C Gironde, 37C Landes) slightly hotter than this morning's estimate but within expectations, shifting winds the main reignition risk, not new growth. Madrid-area fatality count unchanged (one confirmed); Spain bracing for its fourth heat wave of the summer.
stories.score_note: Large-scale humanitarian/disaster story; risk profile remains reignition-risk, not active-growth.

stories.headline: Minnesota AG responds to injunction blocking prediction-market ban; no appeal filed yet
stories.one_line: Minnesota AG Keith Ellison publicly responded to Monday's federal injunction, calling prediction markets 'gambling, plain and simple' and confirming the state will keep defending the law; no notice of appeal reported yet.
stories.score_note: Sector-relevant regulatory thread for prediction-market operators; indirect COIN/HOOD relevance via adjacent market structure.
